messages.text:
Hello,
I received my Hammer DC08 and powered it on. It came with Hammer firmware version 1.0.0 dated 2026-09-12, and Harlo OS was not installed.
I thought Harlo OS was included with the DC08 because Helium Deploy’s Harlo page says it “ships free on every miner we sell, whatever the brand”:
https://heliumdeploy.com/collections/harlo
The D.08 product page is here:
https://heliumdeploy.com/products/hammer-miner-dc08
Could you explain whether Harlo OS was supposed to be preinstalled on my DC08, or whether “ships free” means I’m expected to install it myself?
If I’m meant to install it, please send me the correct DC08 instructions and let me know whether there’s anything I should do before flashing it. I’d also appreciate clarification on why the DC08 arrived with the stock Hammer firmware instead.
Thank you.
Dean
Note to the team: I'll check our notes and both pages before answering.
Read the hammer miner dc08 page
Read the harlo os diagnostics page
Searched the web · harlolabs.com Harlo OS download Hammer DC08

Hi Dean,

Short answer: nothing is missing from your DC08. Harlo OS was never meant to be on it when it left us, so the Hammer 1.0.0 firmware dated 2026-09-12 you are seeing is exactly what that unit ships with from the factory.

Here is what "ships free on every miner we sell" means in practice. Harlo OS is Harlo Labs' own firmware and it is free with every miner we sell, whatever the brand on the case, which is why your order carries the $0 "Harlo OS · Diagnostics + 3-Month RMA" line. Free means no charge and no licence, not preloaded.
It replaces what your miner shipped with, takes about two minutes to install, and it ships preinstalled on the Harlo B30
. The B30 is the one model that arrives with it already on, because it is Harlo's own hardware. Everything else, your DC08 included, arrives on its maker's stock firmware and you flash Harlo OS yourself when you want it. I can see how the collection page reads as "already installed" and I will pass that wording on, since you are not the first person to read it that way.

The good news is that the DC08 is supported. It is on the current compatibility list, alongside the BC04 you already run, so you are not waiting on a profile. For what it is worth, Harlo OS is also our standard answer when a DC08 underperforms on stock firmware, so it is worth doing.

The install, in order.
Open the flasher at harlolabs.com in Chrome or Edge and pick your model, plug in a USB data cable and install, then power on and the self-test runs on its own.
 Pick Hammer DC08 in the model list, not DC06 or DC02. The flasher page also shows the current build, so take the version from there rather than from anything I quote; I would rather you read it live than trust my memory. You will need to take the screen off or reach the USB port directly on the unit, and the cable has to be a real data cable, since a charge-only USB cable is the single most common reason the flasher never sees the miner.

Before you flash, four things. First, write down your pool settings from the stock Hammer interface now, the stratum URL, the port and the worker name, because a factory install wipes the miner's settings and you will be entering them again on the other side. Second, note the hashrate the stock firmware is giving you, so you have a before and after. Third, flash from a computer that will not sleep, keep the miner powered throughout, and do not unplug it while the progress bar is moving. Fourth, Harlo OS is still a public beta, so expect rough edges here and there; after the first install, updates come over the air from Update then Check for Updates, no cable needed again.

One thing to expect: once the DC08 is on Harlo OS it will show the same web interface as your NerdQAxe++ and BC04, so the Depth setting behaviour you reported will very likely appear on it too. That one is already with JD and nothing you do on the DC08 will change it either way.

If anything stalls during the flash, the fastest help is the Harlo OS channel on our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , where you can mention @nullhashrate, who is JD and writes the firmware. Otherwise reply here with where it stopped and I will take it from there.

Best regards,
Hal
